papers.title: PRISM: Predictive Representation of Interaction Style and Motion for Social Robot Navigation
papers.abstract: Humans often observe others before interacting and adjust their behavior accordingly. Robot navigation in crowds, however, often represents pedestrians mainly by observed geometric states, leaving individual differences in interaction tendencies implicit. We propose PRISM (Predictive Representation of Interaction Style and Motion), a framework that infers interaction traits from passive observations of human-human interactions. PRISM encodes human trajectories into a continuous ordinal latent space with a transformer encoder trained by Rank-N-Contrast loss, and pairs each inferred trait with a temporal-stability score supplied to the navigation policy. In randomized crowd simulations, PRISM reduces collision rates over the geometry-only baseline and yields small improvements in navigation-time and path-length metrics. These results suggest the utility of passive latent-trait inference for social navigation in dynamic crowds.

papers.title: PESTO: Formally Correct Registration of LiDAR Point Clouds with Limited Overlap
papers.abstract: In this paper we tackle the problem of aligning LiDAR point clouds also known as the point cloud registration problem. We propose a new algorithm, PESTO, that exploits tetrahedra as "universal features" for LiDAR data, i.e., features that are agnostic to the environment where the LiDAR sensors are deployed. We show empirically that PESTO is competitive with existing solutions for aligning LiDAR point clouds, especially in environments with occlusions. Moreover, we establish PESTO's formal correctness by proving worst-case bounds on the alignment error.

papers.title: Missing Bridges: Composition-Aware Active Imitation Learning
papers.abstract: Active imitation learning reduces expert effort by allowing a learner to request the demonstrations it needs. Existing methods typically select these requests for their expected information gain about the expert policy. In structured multi-task domains, however, the number of start-goal tasks may grow combinatorially despite their solutions sharing reusable behavior. This makes composable behaviors especially valuable, since a single demonstration may help solve many tasks at once. Prior methods do not explicitly account for this value when selecting which demonstration to request. We introduce Adaptive Agents via Latent Topologies (AALT), which requests demonstrations that maximize expected gains in start-goal connectivity. We further show that this objective is formally tied to information gain about task reachability. AALT organizes existing demonstrations into a topology of latent hub states connected by learned behaviors, identifies high-value bridge demonstrations that are likely to enable many tasks at once, and grounds each to an expert query. At inference, it plans through the resulting topology and conditions a diffusion policy on each successive hub transition. In a simulated UR5e robot ordered-retrieval domain with 72 tasks, AALT improved from 42/72 to 72/72 (100%) successful tasks consistently using only 3 demonstrations totaling 5 transitions beyond the initial dataset. After 20 demonstrations, the strongest baseline averaged 88.6% success using 98 transitions.

papers.title: Investigating Adversarial Robustness of Heterogeneous Cooperative Perception
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous cooperative perception (CP) enables connected vehicles with diverse sensor setups to share spatial awareness via compact feature maps, where receivers reconcile these maps using learned translation modules for fusion and inference. Prior attacks against CP in a homogeneous setting reveal that the data exchange introduces a critical attack surface: a single malicious agent can transmit crafted features that erase real objects from a neighbor's fused scene. Yet, it is widely hypothesized that heterogeneity naturally defends against these attacks, as the attacker lacks knowledge of the victim's detector and the translation module scrambles adversarial gradients. We demonstrate that this protection is largely an illusion. Using a matched-objective harness to standardize the perturbation budget, objective, and forward path, we show that properly tuned iterative attacks close or reverse the apparent robustness gap. However, these optimization-based attacks require ground-truth labels and iterative backpropagation, meaning they do not represent a practical field threat running in real-time. To bridge this gap, we introduce HetPoison, a learned generator that crafts a removal perturbation in a single, label-free forward pass. HetPoison transfers across major heterogeneous designs without requiring access to the victim's detector, matching or exceeding the effectiveness of expensive optimizer-based attacks. Since heterogeneity itself is not a defense, we propose HetShield, a lightweight trust layer that validates the spatiotemporal consistency across features, recovering 83--95% of the accuracy degraded by attacks, outperforming prior art.

papers.title: RoboVAD: A Large Cross-Domain Evaluation Benchmark for Anomaly Detection in Robotic Arm Manipulation Videos
papers.abstract: Video anomaly detection (VAD) is an actively studied task, having wide applications in typical scenarios such as public surveillance and road traffic safety. The task is also relevant for robotic arm interactions, where it has several downstream applications, including learning better interaction and manipulation abilities, triggering recovery procedures when anomalies occur, etc. Despite its relevance, the exploration of anomaly detection in robotic arm manipulation videos is limited by the low number of available resources. To this end, we introduce RoboVAD, a large-scale benchmark for video anomaly detection that comprises challenging cross-domain evaluation scenarios, where certain actions (tasks executed by a robotic arm) and anomaly types (mistakes that occur while performing certain tasks) remain unseen during training. RoboVAD is designed to benchmark VAD methods in realistic scenarios, where robotic arms can perform unforeseen tasks, and thereby encounter new anomaly types. We train and evaluate several state-of-the-art VAD methods, including a novel method specifically adapted for robotic arm manipulation. While the proposed method outperforms many state-of-the-art competitors, all methods remain below a micro-averaged frame-level AUC threshold of 70% in the most challenging evaluation setup, confirming the difficulty of the proposed benchmark. We publicly release our dataset and code at this https URL .

papers.title: Imitation Learning for Autonomous Driving in CARLA
papers.abstract: Behavioral cloning trains a policy offline on expert demonstrations, but deployment is closed loop: each action affects the observations the policy receives next. We study how much closed-loop driving competence a compact multimodal policy can acquire from offline demonstrations in the CARLA simulator. The policy uses five-frame histories of RGB images, LiDAR, vehicle telemetry, and lane waypoints to predict throttle, brake, and steering at 20 Hz. Demonstrations were collected in three stages, ending with a systematic route-generation procedure that enumerates spawn points and feasible maneuvers and verifies completed autopilot routes. The released 1.36 million parameter policy was trained on 236,882 windows, representing about 3.3 hours of driving from 448 captures. The resulting policy drives autonomously for hours on training and held-out routes. In our runs, it did so without collisions and also transferred qualitatively to an unseen CARLA town with different road geometry. We also observed recovery from large trajectory deviations, although we do not claim systematic recovery without controlled evaluation. We report offline metrics and distinguish measured results from qualitative closed-loop observations. We release the code, trained checkpoint, ONNX model, data sample, and an evidence audit for the reported claims.

executive_summary: Humanoid and legged loco-manipulation see strong progress, from keyframe-bridged VLM planning and RL whole-body control to adaptive MPC and large-scale traversal learning.
Motion planning advances span multi-robot TAMP optimality, cascade-aware collision risk, kinodynamic planning benchmarks, and LLM-generated MIP formulations for multi-modal planning.
Force-, contact-, and tactile-aware methods are increasingly central for dexterous and contact-rich manipulation, with new VLAs, correction policies, tactile priors, and grasp representations.

Navigation and trajectory planning in dynamic, cluttered, or adverse environments leverage richer risk models, social interaction reasoning, SLAM/mapping innovations, and UAV/quadrotor-specific planners.

Vision-language(-action) models permeate planning and control, guiding keyframes, route planning, world models, and adaptation policies while exposing new challenges in tokenization and real-time execution.

Institution-linked work from CMU, MIT, ETH Zurich, and NYU emphasizes active perception/mobile manipulation, language-grounded route planning, open soft-robot platforms, and reproducible manipulation kits.

institution_matches.title: KINO: A Keyframe Interface for VLM Planning and Whole-Body Control in Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
institution_matches.overview: Introduces a hierarchical humanoid loco-manipulation system where a VLM selects task-relevant whole-body keyframes, which are then retargeted and tracked by a keyframe-conditioned RL controller. A saliency-based keyframe sampling strategy enables large performance gains, achieving up to 92% success on diverse one- and two-handed tasks with a Unitree G1.

institution_matches.title: ActiveScale: Scaling Active Perception for Robots across Model, Data, and Hardware
institution_matches.overview: Proposes an active perception framework for VLAs that augments policies with camera-pose-aware tokens, temporal video inputs, and a mid-training recipe using 1000 hours of egocentric/robotic data. A new mobile-manipulation platform (AMP) supports single-operator teleoperation for large-scale data collection, improving success on viewpoint-dependent manipulation tasks.

institution_matches.title: Map2Route: Benchmarking Compositional Language-Grounded Route Planning over Semantic Maps
institution_matches.overview: Introduces Map2Route, a benchmark of 1,000 episodes testing compositional route planning over semantic maps with rich relational, preference, and constraint language. The accompanying Grounding2Route method converts language into executable code with verification-guided repair, outperforming adapted baselines but still lagging human performance.

institution_matches.title: SPROUT: The Open-Source Soft Growing Robot for Search and Rescue
institution_matches.overview: Releases a fully open soft growing robot system (SPROUT) designed with USAR practitioners for operation in dusty, wet, and confined collapsed-structure environments. Modular hardware and ROS 2 software support varied payloads and control strategies, with field demonstrations of inspection and traversal in first-responder training sites.

institution_matches.title: WetRobo: A Reproducible Robot Kit for Coding Agents in Biological Laboratories
institution_matches.overview: Presents WetRobo, a standardized arm-and-labware kit plus code and demonstrations that allow coding agents to synthesize task programs from natural language without local teleoperation data. In two different labs, a Codex-based agent successfully executes common lab manipulation tasks and transfers better than a lab-specific VLA policy.

institution_matches.title: Not All Layers Need Tuning: Diagnosing and Directing Adaptation in Vision-Language-Action Models
institution_matches.overview: Analyzes where VLAs actually need adaptation under different deployment shifts by measuring per-region parameter displacement and proposing a diagnostic that predicts region importance from a handful of unlabeled target observations. A rank-based LoRA allocator then focuses capacity on key regions, matching or beating uniform adapters and, in real-robot tests, rivaling full fine-tuning with <0.1% of parameters.

topic_matches.title: Learning Holistic Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation with a Bipedal Mobile Manipulator
topic_matches.overview: Trains a unified RL-based whole-body controller that maps 6-DoF end-effector targets directly to coordinated arm and leg actions for a bipedal base, handling reaching, posture adaptation, and stepping without explicit gait commands. A reward-gating scheme and temporal context estimator yield a single policy usable with VR teleoperation, diffusion policies, or scripted goals on hardware.

topic_matches.title: Adaptive-MHE : A Sampling-Based Adaptive MPC for Legged Loco-Manipulation via Moving Horizon Estimation
topic_matches.overview: Combines sampling-based moving-horizon estimation with MPC to identify object and terrain parameters such as mass and friction online for legged loco-manipulation. The framework adapts control to changing conditions without differentiable dynamics, improving robustness over non-adaptive baselines and approaching performance with ground-truth parameters.

topic_matches.title: Learning Multi-Humanoid Pickup and Transport via Decentralized Object-Centric Control
topic_matches.institution: Dynamics Robotics and AI Lab (DRAIL), Oregon State University, Corvallis, OR, USA.
topic_matches.overview: Develops decentralized object-centric policies where each humanoid controls a local attachment region on a shared object, enabling gripperless bimanual pickup, cooperative transport, and handover. Policies trained on single-robot pickup generalize surprisingly well to multi-robot scenarios, with additional gains from explicit multi-humanoid training and successful sim-to-real demonstrations.

topic_matches.title: PASSAGE: Scaling Scene-Aligned Motion Learning for Perceptive Humanoid Traversal in Cluttered Environments
topic_matches.overview: Uses 100 hours of VR-captured, scene-aligned human motion to train a conditional flow-matching planner and a whole-body tracker for humanoid traversal through clutter. The system runs fully onboard with LiDAR mapping and achieves over 70% contact-free success on unseen layouts, composing behaviors like stepping over, ducking, and squeezing past obstacles without skill annotations.

topic_matches.title: ElastiQP: An Always-Feasible QP Solver for Constrained Robot Control
topic_matches.overview: Introduces a dual active-set QP solver that analytically folds L1-penalized slack variables into inequality constraints, guaranteeing a usable solution even when the nominal QP is infeasible. On robot control benchmarks, it matches or exceeds state-of-the-art solvers on feasible problems and delivers valid, minimally violating controls up to 40× faster on infeasible instances, with open-source C++/Python/JAX implementations.

topic_matches.title: Asymptotically Optimal Multi-Robot Task and Motion Planning
topic_matches.overview: Establishes sufficient conditions for asymptotic optimality in multi-robot TAMP where task transitions constrain different robot subsets and thus different subspaces. The proposed planner builds evolving single-robot roadmaps and performs implicit tensor-product search with conditional transition sampling and lazy collision checking, yielding asymptotically optimal multi-robot manipulation plans without constructing the full composite roadmap.

topic_matches.title: CaSCo: Cascade-Aware Soft-Collision Motion Planning
topic_matches.overview: Formulates motion planning that minimizes semantic risk over both direct robot-object and induced object-object collisions using VLM-assigned object risks and physics simulation. Roadmap states are augmented with object arrangements and incurred-risk sets, and an optimal graph search with a cascade-relaxed heuristic finds paths that reason about collision cascades in cluttered manipulation scenes.

topic_matches.title: DynoFluxBench: Benchmarking Kinodynamic Space-Time Planners in Dynamic Environments
topic_matches.overview: Introduces DynoFluxBench, a benchmark for kinodynamic planning in known dynamic environments with unbounded arrival time, and three new planners that fuse kinodynamic and space-time search. The methods are analyzed for probabilistic completeness and empirically compared, with ST-Db-RRT achieving up to 32× faster first-solution times while alternatives remain robust when trajectory optimization is fragile.

topic_matches.title: M$^3$P-R1: Reinforcement Learning for Large Language Model Guided Multi-Modal Motion Planning via MIP Code Generation
topic_matches.overview: Uses RL fine-tuning of LLMs to synthesize executable MIP code for multi-modal motion planning problems that mix continuous dynamics and discrete mode switches. Rather than outputting trajectories directly, the model generates solver-ready Python programs that define variables, constraints, and objectives, learning effective discretizations and coupling constraints from solver feedback.

topic_matches.title: InterMASH: A Unified Geometric Representation for Grasp Synthesis
topic_matches.institution: University of Science and Technology of China
topic_matches.overview: Proposes InterMASH, a cross-embodiment grasp representation based on sphere-anchored tokens whose spherical-harmonic features jointly encode local hand and object geometry plus contact. A conditional diffusion transformer operates on these tokens to generate consistent hand shapes and contacts, achieving competitive physical feasibility on ShadowHand benchmarks and benefiting from joint human–robot training.
